threads.body: Using `VirtualField.find(Consumer.class, String.class)` / `VirtualField.find(Producer.class, String.class)` risks collisions with any other instrumentation that also attaches a `String` virtual field to those same target classes (VirtualField is keyed by target + value type). To avoid accidental sharing/overwrites, use a dedicated value holder type (e.g., an internal `ClusterIdHolder` class) or a small context object instead of `String`.

All reflection failures are swallowed silently, which makes it hard to diagnose why `messaging.kafka.cluster.id` is missing (and can also mask repeated failures that become a performance issue). Consider logging a single debug-level message once per class (or behind an existing 'debug' flag) when reflection fails, while still returning `null` to keep behavior non-fatal.

On the common path where cluster id is not available yet (or reflection fails due to JPMS access restrictions / field name changes), this will retry the full reflective walk on every call, potentially once per span. Consider adding a negative-cache strategy (e.g., store a sentinel plus a 'last attempted' timestamp/backoff) and/or caching reflective lookups (Fields/Methods/MethodHandles) per holder class so repeated failures don't become a hot-path cost.

replies.body:
Both concerns are already addressed:

1. **Negative-cache / sentinel**: When the `metadata` field cannot be found or made accessible, `KafkaClusterId.UNAVAILABLE` (`new KafkaClusterId(null)`) is stored in the VirtualField. Subsequent calls check `cached == KafkaClusterId.UNAVAILABLE` and return `null` immediately without retrying reflection.

2. **Field caching**: `ClassValue<Optional<Field>> metadataFieldCache` runs `getDeclaredField("metadata")` exactly once per holder class (thread-safe, GC-friendly). All subsequent spans use the cached `Optional<Field>` — no repeated reflective lookups.

Hi @laurit, thanks for reviewing the PR. The cluster ID remains constant as long as a cluster is active. However, there are cases where a Kafka cluster might be deleted and recreated with a new cluster UUID while keeping the same broker endpoints. If we don't handle this, it will always pick up the stale UUID, which is why I added this logic.

That said, I discovered that the kafka cluster UUID is already present in the producer and consumer client metadata. I'm going to implement it that way instead, so I will refactor this approach to fetch the cluster UUID from the metadata response.

replies.body:
Good catch, removed in 3ab021b.

You're right that the rule exists — `.github/instructions/java-tests.instructions.md` asks for direct assertions without `.as(...)` descriptions, and `describedAs(...)` is the same AssertJ API under a different name. I'd looked in CONTRIBUTING.md and `docs/contributing/style-guide.md` and wrongly concluded there was no such rule.

Nothing is lost by dropping it: the comment above the loop already records why a pending entry must stay readable, and the test name carries the intent.

threads.body: Concurrent first sends can all observe an empty `VirtualField`, then each `set` and read back its own holder before the next thread writes. That allows every thread to enter the synchronized `Metadata.fetch()` despite the per-holder throttle, and a late initializer can also replace a holder that another thread already resolved. Make publication atomic per client by rechecking and setting while holding a per-client initialization lock (or use an equivalent CAS-capable registry).
